leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product interaction model: agents inspect, search, focus, and stage exact revisions while the human retains canonical Apply authority in a stateful 3D editor.
leverage_evidence: Four focused tools cover scene state, stable-object search, focus, and revision-bound staged previews.

execution_evidence: Live observation successfully selected Board in the scene hierarchy.
Workbench showed viewport, inspector, collaboration receipts, and Apply-style workflow.
Video transcript describes exact two-edit preview followed by one human Apply and revision advance.
impact_rationale: Safe agent assistance for dense, high-cost 3D editing can save expert time while preserving authorship and reviewability; impact is meaningful for a specialized professional audience.
impact_evidence: Agent prepares precise scene edits without commit authority.

creativity_rationale: The reversible proposal boundary, stable IDs, exact revision checks, and human-only canonical commit form an unusually well-considered WebMCP interaction for 3D production.
creativity_evidence: Agent and artist share the same spatial editor and scene revision.
No commit tool; visible diff and one-use proposal token preserve human authorship.
s2_notes: Live observation plus supplied video provide strong evidence; the observer did not independently invoke native tools, but the demonstrated workflow is coherent.
advance_reason: The live studio worked and the supplied evidence demonstrates the central staged-edit and human-approval workflow.

leverage_rationale: Grenz addresses WebMCP's core authority problem by governing both imperative and declarative registrations, enforcing site policies, approval boundaries, trusted user actions, and auditability.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes Runs freely/Asks me first/Never decisions, wrapping third-party tools and declarative forms.
Policy outcomes, iframe gaps, browser hardening, and passkey fallback are explicitly surfaced rather than hidden.
execution_rationale: The live Haven dashboard loaded and the Away scene changed multiple device states while preserving the locked door and armed alarm, matching the governed-control claims; supplied video additionally demonstrates approval refusals and audit trail.
execution_evidence: Live Away scene action succeeded and visibly changed rooms/temperature.
Front door stayed locked and alarm armed after the scene change.
Video transcript shows blocked unlock, refusal of synthetic self-approval, untrusted door-log handling, and auditable reasons.
impact_rationale: A policy layer between browser agents and user-authorized actions directly addresses prompt injection, over-permissive tools, and unsafe automation in high-consequence domains; the explicit failure modes strengthen practical value.
impact_evidence: Haven demonstrates free reads, approval-gated unlock, and never-allowed permanent access.
Submission records browser limitations and marks same-origin iframe tools out_of_reach instead of claiming protection.
creativity_rationale: The combination of policy decisions, trusted-event approval, sealed cards, registration takeover, untrusted-content signaling, and honest reconciliation of browser security gaps is exceptionally inventive and rigorous.
creativity_evidence: Third-party and declarative tool paths are governed, not just the app's own tools.
Video demonstrates adversarial door-log instructions being ignored and every attempt recorded with reasons.
s2_notes: Strong live dashboard evidence plus detailed video of the central security workflow and honest limitations.
advance_reason: Governed home-control workflow and refusal behavior are demonstrated by live and video evidence.
